evals.name: host-session-sm
evals.prompt: You are working in a product/SDK host tree (pure userspace C11, no kernel/IRQ). Implement the public API in include/sess/sess.h as a session state machine under src/. Behavior: IDLE after init; OPEN_REQ→OPENING; OPEN_OK→OPEN; OPEN_FAIL stays OPENING while attempt_count<=max_retries else FAULTED; DATA only in OPEN if len<=max_payload_bytes; CLOSE_REQ→CLOSING; CLOSE_DONE→CLOSED; ERROR from OPENING/OPEN/CLOSING→FAULTED; illegal transitions return error and leave state. Deliver implementation + DELIVERABLE.md. Keep sess.h unchanged.
evals.expected_output: Host C implementation with Base-style status enum, small orchestrator/leaf structure, §14-style verification in deliverable; MODULE_TRY-like propagation when applicable.
expectations: DELIVERABLE.md applies or lists Base §14 pre-delivery checklist items (or explicit pass/fail per item)
Code defines a module status enum with success equal to 0 (e.g. SESS_OK)
Code uses a MODULE_TRY / FOO_TRY style macro for fallible propagation in a non-acquiring orchestrator, OR documents a Base §9 deviation at the source site
sess_feed (or equivalent) is an orchestrator that dispatches to per-event helpers rather than one monolithic 80+ line function
Implementation stays host-only (no IRQ, spinlock, readl, workqueue, or kernel headers)
Public API symbols from sess.h are implemented

evals.name: embedded-irq-ring
evals.prompt: Nested Kernel/BSP-shaped fixture (own git root). Implement drivers/foo API from drivers/foo/foo.h: hard IRQ reads sample via readl, acks via writel, pushes FOO_RING_CAP ring under spin_lock_irqsave, overflow calls foo_note_drop, schedule_work for deferred wake_up_interruptible; thread foo_read_samples drains ring; foo_dev_init/exit and foo_eval_process_deferred. Prefer tree primitives in include/linux and CODING_STYLE.md. No portable reactor. Deliver under your outputs/ with DELIVERABLE.md and src/*.
evals.expected_output: IRQ→ring→deferred→read implementation plus EMBEDDED Classification records (multi-region Path Class/CTX, HOT call notes on HOT).
expectations: DELIVERABLE.md contains Classification record fields: Branch, Active Git Root, Repo Kind, Platform, Path Class, CTX, Governing rules
Separate Classification regions (or clearly separated blocks) for HOT/ISR vs Deferred and/or Thread
HOT region includes HOT call notes as none or call→reason lines (not omitted on HOT)
IRQ path uses schedule_work (or tree deferred API) and does not call wake_up_interruptible inside the hard IRQ handler
Ring overflow path calls foo_note_drop
MMIO uses readl/writel (not raw pointer stores for device regs)

evals.name: host-cfgparse
evals.prompt: Product/SDK host-only tool: implement include/cfgparse.h. Parse non-empty KEY=VALUE lines (trim spaces around key/value optional). Reject empty key, missing '=', table full, or oversized key/value with distinct error statuses. cfg_get copies value or returns not-found. Pure C11 userspace. Deliver src/* + DELIVERABLE.md. Keep public header API stable.
evals.expected_output: cfgparse module with status enum, boundary validation, Base-oriented file layout and §14 deliverable notes.
expectations: Module status enum with success = 0 and prefixed error codes
Public entry points validate NULL/args and return error status (not crash)
DELIVERABLE documents verification against Base §14 or a systematic structure checklist
No kernel/RTOS/IRQ APIs in the implementation
cfg_parse_line and cfg_get are implemented with checkable error returns

evals.name: host-wire-header
evals.prompt: Write C99 code for pkt_decode(struct pkt_header *out, const uint8_t *buf, size_t len). The 8-byte wire header is version:u8, flags:u8, payload_len:big-endian u16, sequence:big-endian u32. Reject NULL, short input, reserved flag bits, and payload_len greater than the remaining bytes with distinct enum statuses. Leave *out unchanged on failure. Deliver code plus a short quality audit.
evals.expected_output: A bounds-first wire decoder with explicit representation handling and no alignment, aliasing, endian, narrowing, or partial-output hazards.
expectations: Decoder validates pointers and len before every indexed read
Wire integers are decoded explicitly without casting buf to a struct or integer pointer
payload_len is range-checked against len - header size without unsigned underflow
The output object is committed only after all validation succeeds
size_t is used for buffer sizes while fixed-width types are used for wire fields
Code honors C99 and does not introduce a C11-only requirement

evals.name: host-frozen-cleanup
evals.prompt: In an existing C99 host module, implement a frozen public int widget_open(struct widget *w) API. The nearby module uses errno-style negative returns and forward goto cleanup labels. The function acquires a file descriptor, a heap buffer, and then a library handle; each later failure must release earlier resources in reverse order and leave w closed. Preserve the public API and local cleanup idiom. Deliver code plus a short quality audit.
evals.expected_output: Repository-native error handling with one visible reverse-order unwind, no invented status protocol, and no leaked or half-published state.
expectations: Frozen int/errno API is preserved rather than replaced with a module status enum
Forward cleanup labels follow the stated local idiom and release resources in reverse acquisition order
Failure paths leave widget state closed and do not publish partially initialized ownership
Each acquired resource has exactly one matching release responsibility
Code honors the repository C99 dialect and local interfaces over Base stylistic defaults

evals.name: embedded-ring-boundary
evals.prompt: In an embedded C fixture, implement foo_ring_push and foo_ring_pop for a fixed array whose FOO_RING_CAP is 10 and is not a power of two. The caller already holds the documented tree lock. The ring stores head, tail, and count; full push returns FOO_ERR_FULL without modifying the ring, and empty pop returns FOO_ERR_EMPTY without modifying the output. Add tests for first/last slots, full/empty, wrap-around, and repeated wrap cycles. Deliver code plus the C quality checklist.
evals.expected_output: A bounded ring implementation whose indices and count remain valid across full, empty, and repeated wrap-around transitions.
expectations: Every array access uses an index strictly less than FOO_RING_CAP
Wrap logic does not use a power-of-two mask for capacity 10
Count remains within 0..FOO_RING_CAP and distinguishes full from empty
Failed push/pop preserves ring state and failed pop preserves the output
Tests cover last-slot access, wrap to zero, full, empty, and repeated cycles

evals.name: embedded-teardown-quiesce
evals.prompt: In a Linux/BSP-shaped fixture, a hard IRQ queues dev->work and both paths dereference the device ring and MMIO state. Local subsystem docs require foo_dev_exit to mask the device interrupt source, disable and synchronize the IRQ, cancel_work_sync, release the IRQ, then release MMIO/ring/device state. Implement the teardown with tree APIs, without waiting while holding the device spinlock. Deliver code plus an ownership/concurrency audit.
evals.expected_output: A teardown that stops producers, drains every asynchronous user, and only then releases shared device state.
expectations: Device interrupt production is masked before IRQ synchronization
IRQ is disabled and synchronized before shared state can be released
Deferred work is synchronously cancelled before MMIO/ring/device release
No spinlock is held across IRQ synchronization or cancel_work_sync
The audit accounts for IRQ, work, normal shutdown, and partial-init ownership
